body:
The partnership, covering the Coller Private Equity Secondaries Fund and Coller Private Credit Secondaries Fund, seeks to address rising demand for sophisticated private markets solutions from Australian wholesale investors.

The private equity secondaries fund offers investors diversified exposure to private equity assets through the acquisition of interests in existing private equity funds and portfolios, while the private credit secondaries fund invests in opportunities across private credit portfolios and transactions, providing access to seasoned credit exposures and the potential for income and diversification.

Luke Mandekic, Co-Head of Distribution at Channel Capital, said the partnership comes as global secondaries continues to solidify itself as an attractive asset class for investors delivering several diversification and liquidity benefits, recording US$226 billion in transaction volumes in 2025.

“Private markets are becoming a more important part of diversified portfolios, and we’re seeing the conversation evolve beyond simply gaining access to the asset class,” he said.

“Many of the advisers we work with are adopting a more sophisticated approach to private markets, combining complementary strategies to build more diversified portfolios for clients.

“Coller EQT brings one of the most established secondaries platforms globally, with deep expertise across both private equity and private credit.

“These strategies offer access to mature private market exposures that can complement traditional allocations and support more deliberate portfolio construction.”

The deal follows in the wake of Coller Capital’s ‘combination’ with global private markets giant EQT AB back in August, buffing up the investment firm’s existing 36-years-strong track record in secondaries investing.

“Globally, we’re witnessing growing recognition of the role secondaries can play alongside traditional private market investments,” Sueann Yeo, Head of Global Wealth Solutions APAC at EQT, said.

“Channel’s strong position in the Australian market makes it a valued partner to help bring greater awareness and support education, access and long-term adoption of secondaries strategies.”

“One of the most significant shifts we are seeing is the growing alignment between institutional and wealth portfolios,” David Hallifax, Director, Global Wealth Solutions APAC at EQT, said.

“Advisers are increasingly seeking the same diversification benefits that have made secondaries a valuable tool for institutional investors, providing exposure across assets, vintages, sectors and geographies. As private markets allocations increase, we expect interest in secondaries to grow alongside them.”
